weeks.weekly_summary: Establishing aerobic base from recent low training volume (6.5 km in 14 days). Build to 35 km with 2 quality sessions spaced throughout the week. Focus: consistency and easy-run economy.
weeks.coaching_notes: Athlete has minimal recent running volume (only 1 run in 2 weeks). Week 1 prioritizes building habit and aerobic foundation without overload. Heart rate data (avg 157 bpm on 6:16/km easy run) confirms current fitness baseline. Two quality sessions (one tempo, one easy-paced progression) introduce structured intensity gently. Recovery run on Wednesday and easy long run on Sunday dial in aerobic system.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 2 increases volume to ~38 km (+8%). Add second tempo session and extend long run to 12 km. Maintain polarized structure.

days.title: Easy 6 km
days.description: Steady aerobic run at easy pace (6:20/km). Focus on relaxed cadence and comfortable breathing. Acclimates the body to consistent running rhythm after low recent volume.
days.notes: Start conservative given limited recent activity. Use this run to establish week 1 consistency.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Active recovery. Light stretching, foam rolling, or easy walk (15–20 min) if desired.

days.title: Tempo 8 km (5 km @ 5:31/km)
days.description: Warm-up 2 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 5 km continuous tempo at lactate threshold pace (5:31/km). Cool-down 1 km easy. This introduces quality intensity and lactate buffering without excessive volume.
days.notes: First hard session of the block. Monitor HR to stay in 75–85% max HR zone. Should feel 'comfortably hard' — conversational pace broken into short phrases.

days.title: Easy Long Run 10 km
days.description: Sustained easy-paced long run at 6:20/km. Focus on aerobic efficiency and mental toughness for distance. Keep HR steady in conversational range throughout.
days.notes: First long run after low recent volume. Finish strong but not exhausted. This sets the foundation for progressive long-run growth.

days.title: Recovery Easy 5 km
days.description: Very easy recovery run at 6:30/km (slightly slower than habitual easy pace). Low HR, minimal stress. Promotes blood flow and aerobic adaptations without fatigue accumulation.
days.notes: Day after long run—keep this short and genuinely easy. Should feel refreshing, not fatiguing.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest or very light cross-training (yoga, walk) if desired.

days.title: Fartlek 6 km (3 × 2 min hard / 2 min easy)
days.description: Warm-up 1 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 3 repetitions of 2 min hard (5:15/km effort) with 2 min recovery easy jog (6:30/km) between. Cool-down 1 km easy. Fartlek format introduces VO2 max stimulus in a playful, less rigid structure.
days.notes: Second quality session of the week. Spaced 4 days from tempo run (Saturday), respecting 2 hard sessions per week limit. Should feel challenging but sustainable.

weeks.weekly_summary: Volume increases to 38 km (+8.6% from Week 1). Two quality sessions maintained; long run grows to 12 km. Polarized structure continues: 80% easy aerobic work, 20% hard intensity. Athlete adapts to running load.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 2 builds on Week 1 momentum. Athlete should feel more confident in aerobic pace and tempo rhythm. Long run extends to 12 km (1.5 km increase from Week 1)—within the 1–2 km/week growth rule. Two quality sessions (tempo + intervals) maintain stimulus for speed development. Recovery run remains present to support aerobic adaptation. Monitor cumulative fatigue; if HR elevated or perceived effort high, dial back intensity.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 3 peaks at ~40 km (+5% from Week 2). Extend long run to 13 km. Add one session with marathon-pace segments (pending future paces). Maintain 2 quality sessions.

days.title: Easy 6 km
days.description: Easy aerobic run at 6:20/km. Consistent pace, conversational breathing. Focus on form and relaxation.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest or light mobility work.

days.title: Tempo 9 km (6 km @ 5:31/km)
days.description: Warm-up 2 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 6 km continuous tempo at 5:31/km lactate threshold pace. Cool-down 1 km easy. Extended tempo builds aerobic-anaerobic bridging and mental resilience.
days.notes: First quality session of Week 2. Should feel slightly easier than Week 1 tempo despite longer duration—athlete has adapted one week of training.

days.title: Easy Long Run 12 km
days.description: Sustained easy-paced long run at 6:20/km. Slow, steady aerobic work. Builds muscular and metabolic endurance. This is the foundation of marathon prep.
days.notes: 2 km increase from Week 1 long run. Finish with energy remaining. Stay hydrated and fueled. This run should feel controlled, not rushed.

days.title: Recovery Easy 5 km
days.description: Very easy recovery run at 6:30/km. Active recovery post-long-run. Low intensity, focus on aerobic blood flow.
days.notes: Day after long run. Keep genuinely easy.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest.

days.title: Intervals 7 km (4 × 1 km @ 5:15/km)
days.description: Warm-up 1.5 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 4 repetitions of 1 km at 5:15/km (VO2 max effort) with 90-second recovery jog (6:30/km) between. Cool-down 1 km easy. VO2 max intervals build cardiovascular power.
days.notes: Second quality session of Week 2. Spaced 4 days from Saturday tempo. Slightly longer intervals than Week 1 fartlek; more structured. Should be hard but controlled—avoid all-out effort.

weeks.weekly_summary: Volume peaks at 40 km (+5% from Week 2). Long run reaches 13 km. Two quality sessions maintained (tempo + intervals). This is the cumulative peak of the block before Week 4 recovery. Athlete should expect elevated but manageable fatigue.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 3 is the hardest week of the block—peak training stimulus before recovery. Long run at 13 km approaches early marathon-distance build. Quality sessions remain robust: 6.5 km tempo and 4.5 km of intervals. Aerobic percentage stays at 80%, enforcing polarized discipline. Monitor HR trends and subjective fatigue; if either is elevated, Week 4 recovery becomes critical. Athlete should feel strong and engaged, not fried.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 4 is RECOVERY: volume drops to ~30 km (−25% from Week 3). Shorten long run to 10–11 km. Keep one quality session (tempo) to maintain speed. Easy runs dial back distance and intensity. This week resets system for next training block.

days.title: Easy 6 km
days.description: Easy-paced aerobic run at 6:20/km. Relaxed form, steady HR in conversational range.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest.

days.title: Tempo 10 km (6.5 km @ 5:31/km)
days.description: Warm-up 2 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 6.5 km continuous tempo at 5:31/km. Cool-down 1.5 km easy. Extended lactate threshold work—tempo should feel firm but sustainable. Focus on running relaxed at threshold pace.
days.notes: Peak intensity session of Week 3. By this point, athlete has 3 weeks of consistent training. Tempo pace should feel solid, not desperate. Maintain strong form throughout.

days.title: Easy Long Run 13 km
days.description: Sustained easy-paced long run at 6:20/km. 13 km builds genuine endurance and mental fortitude. Fueling strategy: consume sports drink or gels around 60 min mark (e.g., 6–6.5 km in). This is the longest run of the block.
days.notes: 1 km increase from Week 2 long run. By Week 3, athlete should be comfortable at this distance. Finish with energy. This run is the lynchpin of the block's aerobic development.

days.title: Recovery Easy 5 km
days.description: Very easy recovery run at 6:30/km. Post-long-run active recovery. Minimal effort.
days.notes: Day after 13 km long run. Keep short and relaxed.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest.

days.title: Intervals 8 km (5 × 1 km @ 5:15/km)
days.description: Warm-up 1.5 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 5 repetitions of 1 km at 5:15/km (VO2 max effort) with 90-second recovery jog (6:30/km) between. Cool-down 1 km easy. Fifth 1 km rep—add one extra rep compared to Week 2 to build VO2 capacity.
days.notes: Second quality session of Week 3. Spaced 4 days from Saturday tempo. Five reps is challenging; focus on controlled effort, not all-out burning. By rep 5, effort should still feel controlled at target pace.

weeks.weekly_summary: RECOVERY WEEK: Volume drops to 30 km (−25% from Week 3 peak). Long run shortened to 10.5 km. One quality session maintained (tempo, 5 km) to preserve speed. Rest days and easy runs dominate. System resets; prepare for next training block.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is critical recovery. Cumulative fatigue from 3 weeks of progressive build is managed by significant volume reduction. HR should normalize; perceived effort drops. One tempo session (5 km core) maintains lactate threshold without overload. Long run drops to 10.5 km (20% reduction from Week 3). Rest days increased. Athlete may feel 'flat' or sluggish this week—this is normal and necessary for adaptation. By week's end, system will be recharged and ready for next block's progression.
weeks.next_week_preview: Following this block, athlete should reassess fitness via easy pace run and re-test tempo effort. If no race date is set, recommend establishing target marathon date and fitness markers (target MP, VO2 pace). Next block: Aerobic Development phase (weeks 5–8) builds marathon-pace work and longer tempos.

days.title: Easy 5 km
days.description: Easy-paced run at 6:20/km. Relax and enjoy the reduced volume. Light effort.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest.

days.title: Tempo 7 km (5 km @ 5:31/km)
days.description: Warm-up 1 km easy (6:20/km). Main set: 5 km continuous tempo at 5:31/km. Cool-down 1 km easy. Shortened tempo (compared to Week 3) maintains lactate threshold while reducing fatigue load.
days.notes: Recovery week quality session. Pace is same (5:31/km) but shorter duration. Should feel good; athlete may surprise self with ease at threshold pace after a recovery week.

days.title: Easy Long Run 10.5 km
days.description: Sustained easy-paced long run at 6:20/km. Recovery long run—reduced from 13 km. Finish fresh; this is about maintaining endurance base without adding new stress.
days.notes: 20% reduction from Week 3 long run (13 km → 10.5 km). Keep effort conversational. Should finish feeling energized, not depleted.

days.title: Easy 4 km
days.description: Very short, very easy recovery run at 6:30/km. Flush legs post-long-run. Minimal volume, minimal stress.
days.notes: Shortest easy run of the week. Day after long run; keep it light.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest.

days.title: Easy 4.5 km
days.description: Easy-paced run at 6:20/km. Final run of the recovery week. Light, casual effort. Feel the adaptation happening.
days.notes: End-of-week easy run. By this run, athlete should feel fresher. If HR is elevated or perceived effort high, add an extra rest day post-block.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes aerobic foundation and introduces quality intensity work for an athlete with minimal recent running volume (6.5 km in 14 days). Week 1 (35 km) restarts consistent training with 2 quality sessions (tempo + fartlek). Week 2 (38 km) adds volume (+8.6%) and extends the long run to 12 km. Week 3 (40 km) peaks at +5% from Week 2, with longest run at 13 km and VO2 max intervals. Week 4 (30 km) is recovery, dropping volume −25% with shortened long run (10.5 km) and reduced tempo. Polarized structure (80% easy, 20% hard) maintained throughout. Training paces anchored to current Strava fitness: Easy/Long Run at 6:20/km (slight buffer above 6:16/km current pace), Tempo at 5:31/km, VO2 max intervals at 5:15/km. No race date set—after this block, athlete should establish marathon target date and schedule upcoming Aerobic Development phase (weeks 5–8) with marathon-pace work. Total block distance: 143 km.
